subject: science
passage: The oldest known living tree (a Great Basin bristlecone pine that researchers have nicknamed ______ grows high in the White Mountains of eastern California and has been alive for more than 4,800 years. Bristlecones grow slowly in thin, dry soil near the tree line, and their dense, resin-rich wood resists rot and insects. Even a tree that is mostly dead can keep a thin strip of living bark alive for centuries, which is one reason these twisted, weather-beaten pines outlast nearly every other living thing on Earth.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A Great Basin bristlecone pine that researchers have nicknamed Methuselah" is extra information that opens with a parenthesis after "tree." It must close with a matching parenthesis before the verb "grows."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Without a closing parenthesis, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "grows."
explanation.B: Incorrect. The extra information opens with a parenthesis, so it can't close with a comma; the two marks must match.
explanation.C: Correct. The closing parenthesis matches the opening one and completes the pair around the extra information.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The closing parenthesis is right, but the comma after it separates the subject "The oldest known living tree" from its verb "grows."
